messages:
Maria G: Heads up — since ~03:40 UTC EU SSO logins intermittently fail. SCIM shows users created but RBAC mapping missing. Verifier service logs 'signature verification failed'. Anyone seen timezone/attribute normalization cause signature issues?
Devon: Can you paste a sanitized assertion + the verifier log lines you see?
Maria G: pasted sanitized snippet + logs:
```xml
<saml:Attribute Name="timezone">
  <saml:AttributeValue>Europe/London</saml:AttributeValue>
</saml:Attribute>
<saml:Attribute Name="roles">
  <saml:AttributeValue>team:eng:admin</saml:AttributeValue>
</saml:Attribute>
```
logs:
```
2026-03-22T03:41:12Z verifier ERROR: signature verification failed: rsa_pkcs1_verify: wrong public key
2026-03-22T03:41:12Z verifier TRACE: signed_info_digest: abc123def456... kid: alias/idp-2026-03
```
Devon: kid looks ok. Two quick suspects: 1) IdP rotated the signing key (KMS) or changed signature params (PSS vs PKCS1). 2) XML canonicalization differences (whitespace/line endings) between what IdP signed and what verifier canonicalizes.
Alex: check the assertion's SignatureMethod and CanonicalizationMethod in the signedinfo. If the IdP lib switched to different C14N or added xml:lang/whitespace, digest changes. Also KMS can emit different signature formats depending on call params.
Maria G: pulled raw assertion for a failing and a succeeding request. The only byte diff I can see is a CRLF right before the <ds:Signature> block on failures. Example (redacted): `...</AttributeValue>
  <ds:Signature xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#">`
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-031 — https://incidents/reports/INC-2026-031 :eyes: 
Alex: that CRLF clue screams canonicalization mismatch. If IdP signs a version with LF-only but our verifier reads CRLF-pretty-printed XML (or vice versa) the digest won't match. Also confirm whether the IdP is signing the raw XML before any formatting/transport wrapper.
security-eng: temporary mitigation: add a tolerant normalization step that normalizes CRLF->LF prior to canonicalize+verify. Add extra audit logging (assertion_id, digest, trace id) so we can correlate. We'll want this behind a feature flag for canary.
Devon: I can implement normalize_newlines() in verifier and gate it behind rsig.tolerate_lf flag set to 10% traffic. Also will add a debug dump to S3 with trace id inc-2026-031 if verification fails.
oncall-bot: @Devon please run staging tests and capture a full SAML with trace id. Command: `/tools/samltool verify --trace inc-2026-031 --raw-assertion /tmp/assertion.b64`
Devon: quick note — logs show 'wrong public key' as well. Could be cert/cache mismatch: our cert cache might still have the old cert while metadata updated. Try forcing metadata refresh on verifier.
Alex: good call. Do `POST /_admin/keys/refresh` on verifier and compare stored cert fingerprint to IdP metadata: `openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256 -in idp.crt`. If KMS alias rotated, kid should change.
security-eng: also add an alert rule: signature_verif_fail > 5 per minute -> P1 and ensure audit events include affected user ids and RBAC mapping state.
Maria G: action items: 1) @Devon push tolerant patch to canary (10%). 2) I'll contact IdP provider to ask about any lib/format changes or KMS key rotations and request they include CanonicalizationMethod/SignatureMethod in metadata. 3) @Alex force cert refresh and compare fingerprints. 4) @security-eng add alert & audit entries. I'll attach list of 23 affected user ids to INC-2026-031.
Devon: pushed canary patch (rsig.tolerate_lf=10%). Early canary logs: 1 failing -> after normalization verify succeeds. Uploaded debug trace inc-2026-031-1 to S3 for analysis.
sre-bot: Deploy bot: canary deploy succeeded 2026-03-22T04:10Z
Maria G: thanks all — I'll update after IdP support replies. :thumbsup:
